varieties.name: Moroccan
varieties.season: 35-40 days to maturity in summer; 45-50 days in winter
varieties.traits: Vigorous, fast-growing, high heat tolerance for a single cut; bolts sooner than the slow-bolting types, so cannot be left standing long in the field; smaller leaf (1-3mm), dark green, fast germination
varieties.note: Starke Ayres commercial cultivar. Zones assigned as this pass's inference for cooler-season/shorter-window production (it 'can easily be grown all year' but is explicitly NOT a slow-bolt choice), distinct from Green Aroma/American Long which the source itself ties to 'mild and subtropical climates'.

evidence.quote: Coriander Moroccan a one cut with a very good heat tolerance. Its vigorous and performance is excellent during hot summer. It can easily be grown all the year.
evidence.doc: Coriander Moroccan Seeds, Starke Ayres product page

evidence.quote: Maturity Summer: 35 to 40 days. Winter: 45 to 50 days. Plant Characteristics Plants are vigorous and fast growing therefore they can bolt sooner.
evidence.doc: Coriander Moroccan Seeds, Starke Ayres product page

evidence.quote: MOROCCAN is an early maturing variety that can handle the heat in summer. You can not leave the plant for to long in the field.
evidence.doc: Coriander Moroccan Seeds, Starke Ayres product page

varieties.name: Green Aroma
varieties.season: 40 days to maturity in summer; 50-55 days in winter
varieties.traits: Tall standing, slow (late) bolting type; grows well in mild and subtropical climates; good adaptability for year-round production 'in certain areas'; young leaves/stems have relatively mild aroma
varieties.note: Explicitly named for mild/subtropical climates in the source — zones assigned to those matching that climate description under the brief's zone key. This is the cultivar to prefer over Moroccan for a longer standing window before bolting.

evidence.quote: Green Aroma is a long standing all-year variety. It is a tall standing type plant, with slow bolting. Plants grow well in mild and subtropical climates.
evidence.doc: Coriander Green Aroma Seeds, Starke Ayres product page

evidence.quote: This variety shows good adaptability for year round production in certain areas.
evidence.doc: Coriander Green Aroma Seeds, Starke Ayres product page

varieties.name: American Long (Standing)
varieties.season: 40 days to maturity in summer; 50-55 days in winter
varieties.traits: Tall standing, slow (late) bolting type; grows well in mild and subtropical climates; good adaptability for year-round production 'in certain areas'
varieties.note: Near-identical description and same source/zone reasoning as Green Aroma — both are the 'slow-bolt' pair Starke Ayres pitches against the fast-bolting Moroccan.

evidence.quote: American Long Standing is an all-year variety. It is a tall standing type plant, with slow bolting. Plants grow well in mild and subtropical climates.
evidence.doc: Coriander American Long Seeds, Starke Ayres product page

subtropical-coast.text: Best-sourced fit: Green Aroma or American Long, both explicitly described as suited to 'mild and subtropical climates' with slow bolting and year-round production potential.

lowveld-bushveld.text: Same reasoning as subtropical-coast — mild/subtropical-climate cultivars are this pass's inferred fit, not separately confirmed by the source for this specific zone by name.

southern-cape.text: Same reasoning as subtropical-coast (mild coastal climate) — inferred fit, not source-confirmed by name.

highveld.text: Moroccan is this pass's fit for a quick single cut ahead of hot, dry highveld summer conditions given its explicit heat tolerance, accepting that it bolts sooner and needs prompt harvest — not source-confirmed by zone name.

midlands-mistbelt.text: Same reasoning as highveld for Moroccan — inferred, not source-confirmed by zone name.

gaps: None of the three Starke Ayres cultivar pages names a South African province, region or climate zone directly — every zone assignment above is this pass's own inference from the stated 'mild/subtropical climate' vs 'heat tolerant, one-cut' framing, flagged in each note.
No sourced recommendation at all for western-cape, karoo-arid or high-mountain.
